prompt: Animate the player (idle, run, jump, fall) using an AnimationTree with a state machine.

config.plan_model: Agent-tool model parameter 'sonnet' (Claude Code sub-agent; the harness did not report the resolved model id)
config.how: one fresh general-purpose sub-agent per plan, reads a job file with project brief + the developer prompt, writes numbered plan (<=8 steps, no code) via Write; not Claude Code plan mode

plans.text:
1. Read player.gd and the Player scene to learn how movement, jumping, and gravity are handled, and what signals or properties (velocity, is_on_floor) can drive the animation states.
2. Check how the Sprite2D is set up (single texture vs. sprite sheet, frame size, hframes/vframes) and confirm the art assets for idle, run, jump, and fall exist or note which are missing.
3. Add an AnimationPlayer to the Player scene and create four animations (idle, run, jump, fall), setting frame tracks on the Sprite2D, loop modes, and speeds appropriate to each.
4. Add an AnimationTree node, point it at the AnimationPlayer, and set its root to an AnimationNodeStateMachine with the four animations as states.
5. Define the transitions between states (idle to run, run to idle, any grounded state to jump, jump to fall, fall to idle or run on landing) with sensible switch modes and conditions or advance expressions.
6. Update player.gd to activate the tree, get its state machine playback, and each physics frame travel to the correct state from velocity and floor contact, also flipping the sprite based on horizontal direction.
7. Test in level_01.tscn by running the level and exercising walking, jumping, falling off ledges, and landing, watching for flicker, wrong states, or stuck transitions, and tune transitions accordingly.
8. Confirm the enemy scenes and the rest of the level are unaffected, and tidy up any unused nodes or debug output.

1. Inspect player.gd and the Player scene to learn how movement, jumping, and gravity are currently handled, and which signals or properties (velocity, is_on_floor) can drive animation state.
2. Prepare the sprite art: confirm the Sprite2D spritesheet has frames for idle, run, jump, and fall, and note the frame count and timing for each.
3. Add an AnimationPlayer to the Player scene and create four animations (idle, run, jump, fall) that key the Sprite2D frame, with looping set on idle and run and not on jump and fall.
4. Add an AnimationTree node to the Player scene, point it at the AnimationPlayer, and set its root to an AnimationNodeStateMachine.
5. In the state machine, add idle, run, jump, and fall states, then connect them with transitions (idle/run, any grounded state to jump, jump to fall, fall back to idle/run), choosing switch modes and conditions or auto-advance as appropriate.
6. Update player.gd to fetch the state machine playback object and travel to the correct state each physics frame based on floor contact, vertical velocity, and horizontal input, also flipping the sprite to face movement direction.
7. Activate the AnimationTree and make sure the player script no longer plays animations directly, so there is a single source of animation control.
8. Run level_01.tscn to test every transition (standing, running, jumping, falling off ledges, landing), then tune transition timing and fix any flicker or stuck states.

1. Review player.gd and the Player scene to see how movement, jumping, and gravity are handled, and note the signals available for deciding idle, run, jump, and fall (velocity and is_on_floor).
2. Prepare the sprite art: confirm or slice the Sprite2D sheet into idle, run, jump, and fall frames, and decide frame counts, timing, and whether the sprite needs flipping for facing direction.
3. Add an AnimationPlayer as a child of Player and create four animations (idle, run, jump, fall) that key the Sprite2D frame properties, setting looping on idle and run and one-shot or hold behavior on jump and fall.
4. Add an AnimationTree node to Player, point it at the AnimationPlayer, and set its root to a state machine, leaving it inactive until the setup is complete.
5. Build the state machine with idle, run, jump, and fall states, and add transitions: idle and run switching on horizontal speed, any grounded state to jump on upward velocity, jump to fall at the apex, and fall back to idle or run on landing.
6. Update player.gd to fetch the state machine playback object, and each physics frame drive travel to the correct state from floor contact and velocity, while flipping the sprite according to input direction.
7. Activate the AnimationTree, and make sure the AnimationPlayer is not also being played directly from player.gd so the two do not fight over the sprite.
8. Run level_01.tscn to test each state (standing, running both directions, jumping, falling off a ledge, landing), watch for flicker or stuck states, and tune transition conditions and blend times.

1. Inspect player.gd and the Player scene to learn how movement, gravity, jumping and floor detection are currently handled, and which signals or properties (velocity, is_on_floor) can drive animation state.
2. Gather or create the sprite frames for idle, run, jump and fall, and decide whether to animate the Sprite2D via frame/region tracks or switch to an AnimatedSprite2D; keep the existing CollisionShape2D unchanged.
3. Add an AnimationPlayer to the Player scene and author four animations (idle and run looping, jump and fall non-looping or holding their last frame) with consistent frame rates and sprite flipping handled separately.
4. Add an AnimationTree node, point it at the AnimationPlayer, set its root to an AnimationNodeStateMachine, and activate it.
5. In the state machine, add Idle, Run, Jump and Fall states each referencing its animation, then add transitions: Idle to Run, Run to Idle, Idle and Run to Jump, Idle and Run to Fall (walking off ledges), Jump to Fall, and Fall to Idle or Run on landing.
6. Configure each transition's switch mode, advance condition or expression, and a short crossfade, so grounded/velocity checks decide changes and Jump-to-Fall triggers at the apex when vertical velocity turns positive.
7. Update player.gd to fetch the state machine playback object, and each physics frame travel to the matching state from is_on_floor, horizontal velocity and vertical velocity, while flipping the sprite based on facing direction.
8. Playtest in level_01.tscn covering standing, running, jumping, falling off platforms, landing and direction changes, then fix timing, loop settings and transition glitches found.

1. Review player.gd and the Player scene to learn how movement, jumping, and gravity are currently handled, and note which values (velocity, is_on_floor, facing direction) will drive the animation states.
2. Confirm the Sprite2D's spritesheet layout (frame size, frame counts for idle, run, jump, fall) and set up its hframes/vframes or swap to an AnimatedSprite2D only if the sheet requires it.

4. Add an AnimationTree node to the Player scene, point it at the AnimationPlayer, and set its tree root to a new AnimationNodeStateMachine.
5. In the state machine, create idle, run, jump, and fall states and wire the transitions: idle and run in both directions, either of them to jump, jump to fall, and fall back to idle or run on landing.
6. Define transition conditions (for example on-floor, moving, rising) as AnimationTree parameters so the tree can be driven from script rather than by travel calls scattered through the code.
7. Update player.gd to activate the tree, set those parameters each physics frame from velocity and floor state, and flip the sprite horizontally based on facing direction.
8. Run level_01.tscn and test every transition, including walking off a ledge, jumping, landing, and quick direction changes, then tune transition timing and fix any flicker or stuck states.
